title: English Podcast For Learning English Conversation | How To Talk About Your Daily Routine
short: How To Talk About Your Daily Routine

sentences.t: Hello and welcome back to Leo English podcast.
It's so good to see you again today.
Hello everyone. Welcome back to our little English class.
I'm Tina.
And I'm Leo.
Our channel is for English learners like you.
We talk about normal everyday life, the things you actually do, the things you actually say.
We use simple English around A2 to B1 level, so you can follow the whole conversation without stopping.
And our goal is very simple.
We want you to speak, not just read grammar rules and feel sleepy.
Right. Reading is good, speaking is better.
That's a very short slogan.
I like it.
Thank you. I practice these at home.
Today's topic is my favorite topic, honestly.
We are talking about your daily routine.
Your daily routine.
What you do from morning till night.
When you wake up, what you eat, how you go to work, when you sleep.
And why is this so useful?
I'll tell you why.
Because this topic comes up in almost every English conversation.
New friend, they ask, "What do you do every day?"
Job interview, "Tell me about your typical day."
Language exam, "Describe your daily routine."
It's everywhere.
Exactly. And here is the nice thing.
You don't need difficult grammar for this.
You need the present simple tense.
I wake up, I eat, I go.
And some time words.
First, then, after that, usually, sometimes.
Present simple and time words.
That's the whole magic.
So today we will walk through one full day, hour by hour, from 6:00 in the morning to 11:00 at night.
And I will tell you my routine, which is a little chaotic, and Tina will tell you her routine, which is very organized.
You will see the difference.
It's a big difference, believe me.
Before we start, if you enjoy this kind of lesson, please give us a like.
It really helps.
And please subscribe.
We make new lessons every day about real conversations in real life.
Okay, let's talk about mornings.
Let's talk about alarms.
Let's talk about my enemy, the alarm clock.
Let's get started.
So, Leo, how are you today?
I'm good, but I'm a little sleepy, honestly.
I went to bed very late last night.
What time?
Around 1:30 in the morning.
I was watching a video about how to sleep better.
[sighs and gasps]
You watched a video about sleeping, and then you didn't sleep.
Yes, it was a very good video.
Too good. I watched three of them.
How ironic.
What does ironic mean again?
It means a situation that is strange or funny because it's the opposite of what you expect.
You watched videos about sleep and lost sleep.
That's ironic.
Ah. So, my whole life is ironic.
And how are you?
You look very awake.
I am awake, thank you.
I woke up at 6:00, I went for a short walk, and I made a list for today.
A list? Of course, you always have a list.
I have three lists.
One for today, one for this week, one for my life.
One for my life?
That's terrifying.
So, what did you do this weekend?
On Saturday, I tried to clean my apartment.
I started at 10:00 in the morning, then I found an old box of photos at 11:00, and I sat on the floor looking at photos until 2:00
in the afternoon.
So, you cleaned for 1 hour?
I cleaned the box.
The box is very clean now.
And Sunday?
Sunday was better.
I cooked dinner for my sister.
I made pasta and I only burned one thing.
Only one thing, very good.
It was the bread, but the pasta was excellent.
My sister said, "Wow, you can cook."
And I said, "Yes, I know."
And then she said, "Don't lie to me, Leo."
She knows you too well.
She does. My weekend was small and quiet.
I went to the market.
I bought vegetables and I read a book on Sunday evening.
You read a book in the evening.
That sounds nice.
It was nice.
I read for 1 hour and then I went to bed at 10.
10 on a Sunday?
10. And I slept 8 hours.
And on Monday, I felt like a new person.
See, I want that, but my brain at 11 at night says, "Leo, let's do something fun."
And my brain at 7:00 in the morning says, "Leo, let's not."
Speaking of brains and mornings and evenings, that is exactly our topic today.
It is. The daily routine.
The story of my life hour by hour.
And notice something.
In this warm-up, we already used a lot of routine language.
I will up at 6:00.
I went to bed at 10:00 on Saturday in the evening.
Oh, you're right.
We were already practicing.
So, let's do it properly now.
One full day.
Start at the beginning.
At the alarm.
At the alarm.
Okay, Leo. It's 6:00 in the morning.
What happens?
Nothing happens. I am not there.
What do you mean you're not there?
I mean it's 6:00 in the morning.
I am not a person.
I am a blanket with a small face.
Okay, so at 6:00 in the morning you don't wake up.
When is your alarm?
I have four alarms.
Four alarms?
Four. And here's the problem.
I don't remember turning them off.
So you turn them off in your sleep?
In my sleep, like a machine.
My hand knows the way to the phone.
My brain is not invited.
Oh, I do that too sometimes, but not four times.
I'm not a champion.
Thank you. I'll take that as a compliment.
So what time do you really wake up?
Around 7:15, and then I have 20 minutes to do everything.
Shower, clothes, teeth, phone, keys, out.
20 minutes for everything?
That sounds stressful.
It is, and that's why I have a rule for myself.
I keep three shirts ready.
I keep my bag near the door, and I keep my keys in the same place every single day.
That's actually smart.
It's not smart, it's survival.
I won't spend 15 minutes looking for my keys while holding them.
Holding them? Where?
In my hand, the whole time.
I was looking for keys and my keys were in my hand.
That's a very human moment.
Thank you. So when do you wake up, Tina?
At 6:00. Sometimes 5:50, but I don't set my alarm for 5:50.
That would be strange.
How many alarms?
One. Do you know how much I hate you right now?
One alarm and I put my phone in the kitchen, so when the alarm rings, I have to stand up and walk to turn it off.
Oh, that's clever, because you can't reach it from the bed.
Exactly. My body is already standing, so I just stay up.
In the morning, standing up is the hardest part.
After that, it's easy.
Standing up is the hardest part.
So simple, so painful.
And what's the first thing you do in the morning?
Check my phone immediately before I stand up.
Me too, unfortunately, but I read that we shouldn't do that.
You read it, I read it, we all read it, and we all do it.
Every morning I do this.
I open my eyes, I take my phone, and I look at messages.
And then I feel a little stressed before I even drink water.
What's the first thing you drink?
Water. One big glass of water before coffee.
Water before coffee?
That's discipline.
The body is dry after 8 hours of sleep.
So, water first, then coffee.
My routine is coffee first, then regret.
What kind of coffee do you drink?
Black, no sugar, very strong.
I make it at home because I'm always late, and the coffee shop near my building has a long line.
How much coffee do you drink in a day?
Two cups in the morning, one in the afternoon, maybe three.
Don't judge me.
I drink one, and if I drink two, I can't sleep at night.
Really? Even one cup after 12:00?
No, even at 11:00 in the morning.
My body is sensitive.
I sleep badly.
That's so different for me.
I can drink coffee at 9:00 in the evening and sleep like a baby.
I envy you.
So, breakfast. Do you eat breakfast?
I eat breakfast standing up, usually toast, sometimes bread and cheese, on very good days, a banana.
A banana is a very good day?
It's a big deal, Tina.
It's colorful. It has vitamins.
And you eat while you're getting dressed?
Yes, and sometimes I eat my toast on the way to the bus stop, eating, walking, and looking at my phone.
Three things at the same time.
That's not eating.
That's an activity.
Yes, activity is the correct word.
So, breakfast for you?
I eat breakfast sitting down every day.
Usually eggs and some bread with vegetables, and I never watch my phone while I eat.
Never for the first 10 minutes.
I read that eating slowly is important for the body and the mind.
That sounds like a nice 10 minutes.
It is. It's my favorite 10 minutes of the day.
Quiet, slow, and warm.
Wow, my favorite 10 minutes of the day is at 10 at night when I'm on the sofa with ice cream.
Let's talk about the commute.
How do you go to work?
By bus, about 35 minutes.
Then I walk 5 minutes from the bus stop.
Bus or subway, which is better?
Hmm, the subway is faster, but the bus is more interesting.
On the bus, you can see the city, and sometimes you see a dog.
The subway has no dogs.
That's a very strong opinion.
It's a real opinion.
So, how do you go to work?
I walk. I walk 20 minutes.
Rain, sun, cold, every day.
Even in the cold?
Even in the cold.
I wear a good coat.
20 minutes of walking is my exercise, and it's free.
Free exercise. Look at you, so productive.
What do you do on the bus?
Do you sleep?
Sometimes. Once I slept and missed my stop, and I told my manager, "The bus forgot to stop."
And he said, "The bus did not forget, Leo."
Did he believe you?
He's been generous about my excuses, but I think he writes them down.
So, what time do you arrive at work?
Around 9:00. Sometimes a little after 9:00.
My manager starts at 9:00, so sometimes I see his face at the elevator, and I say, "Good morning," and I hide behind my coffee.
And you? I arrive at 8:40, 10 minutes before the office day starts at 9:00.
10 minutes early, why?
Because I like the quiet minutes before everyone comes.
I sit down, I open my notebook, and I write my three most important tasks for today.
Three tasks, that's a good idea.
It's a very good idea.
Not 10 tasks, three.
Because if you write 10, you finish two, and then you feel bad.
I write 10 tasks, and I finish zero.
And I look at the list, and I feel sick.
So, try three.
Okay. What happens in your morning at work?
First, I read my emails, then I make a cup of tea, then I start my most important task before lunch because morning is my best time.
What does best time mean exactly?
It means the time when my brain works best.
Some people are morning people, some people are night people.
I'm a morning person.
I'm a night person, a 3:00 a.m.
person, my sister says.
What do you do at work in the morning?
Emails first, then meetings, usually one or two meetings in the morning, and then I feel like I did a lot,
but I didn't.
I just talked.
Talking is work sometimes.
Sometimes, but my real work is on my screen, design work.
And design work needs quiet.
So, my best time is actually after 5:00 when everyone goes home.
Oh, I see.
When the office is quiet.
Yes, it's strange.
I'm tired, but I can work, and the ideas come easily.
I read something about this.
Some people feel more creative in the evening.
It's about the body clock.
The body clock?
What does body clock mean?
It's the natural clock inside your body.
It tells you when to sleep and when to be awake.
My body clock is broken.
It says party at midnight and sleep at 9:00 in the morning.
So, lunch. What time do you eat?
Between 12:30 and 1:00.
Usually in the office kitchen with three or four colleagues.
Where do you eat?
At my desk, usually.
Which is a bad habit, actually.
Really? You? Bad habit?
Yes, me. I eat and I read email at the same time, and I finish lunch in 10 minutes.
And then I feel like I didn't eat.
10 minutes? I eat slowly.
25, 30 minutes, sometimes 35.
Food is important.
Do you eat with people?
Sometimes, but at least once a week I eat alone.
Just me and my food.
No phone.
That's nice. I should do that.
What do you usually eat?
A rice bowl with vegetables and chicken.
Sometimes soup. I cook on Sunday and I bring lunch every day.
Every day? You cook for the whole week?
On Sunday I cook three or four different things.
Then I put them in boxes and I freeze some.
I tried that once.
I cooked for the whole week on Sunday, and on Wednesday I had no food left.
I don't know what happened.
What do you mean you don't know?
I mean I ate it in two days.
On Monday and Tuesday I ate a week of food in two days.
That's actually impressive.
Thank you. And what about my afternoon?
After lunch at 2:00 everybody is sleepy.
Everybody. What do you do?
I drink water, I stand up, I walk around the office, and I look out the window for 2 minutes.
That's very healthy.
Yes, and then I drink coffee.
It's not perfect, but the walking helps.
The coffee is my backup plan.
What time do you finish work?
Officially 6:00, really 6:30 or 7:00, sometimes 8:00.
That's a long day.
Yes. And you?
5:30, and I leave at 5:30, every day.
Really? You stop exactly when the clock says?
I try, because if I stay one extra hour every day, then in one month, I work 20 extra hours,
and nobody thanks me.
I never thought about it like that.
Also, I'm more useful in the morning.
Staying late is not productive for me.
My brain is finished at 6.
I love that.
My brain is finished at 6.
So, after work, what do you do?
I don't go home immediately.
I like to walk for 15 minutes first.
Then I go to the gym two times a week, Monday and Thursday.
You go to the gym?
That's a surprise.
Why is it a surprise?
Because you have a very relaxed personality.
I didn't expect it.
Relatives also don't believe it, but it's true.
I go Monday and Thursday from 7:00 to 8:00, and I feel very good after.
But before, I don't want to go.
That's what everybody says.
The hardest part is going.
Yes, the hardest part is not the exercise.
The hardest part is the shoe.
The shoe?
The first shoe.
When the first shoe is on, the second shoe is easy.
So, I tell myself, Leo, just put on one shoe, and then it's done.
That's a great trick, honestly.
It works. What about you?
Walking is my exercise, and I do 20 minutes of stretching at home in the evening while I listen to a podcast.
Do you listen to English podcasts?
Because I know a very good one.
Yes, I know that one.
So, dinner. What time do you eat?
Around 8:00 or 8:30, sometimes 9:00.
I know that's late.
What do you cook?
Simple things. Rice with eggs or pasta or a soup from my mother's recipe.
I can make three soups.
My mother makes 40.
Do you eat alone or with family?
Usually alone on weekdays.
Sometimes I call my sister while I cook and she says, "Are you burning something?"
because she can hear the pan.
Can she?
Yes, she can hear the pan.
That's what love is.
And dinner for you?
At 7:00, usually something light.
Fish or chicken with vegetables because if I eat a big dinner at 9:00, I can't sleep.
This is a very important point.
Food and sleep are connected.
Very connected. After a big late dinner, the body is still working.
You sleep badly and the next morning you feel heavy.
Heavy is the perfect word.
That's how I feel every morning, heavy.
So, after dinner, what do you do?
I sit on the sofa and I watch something.
Then at around 10:00, I say, "Okay, I'll sleep at 11:00."
And then at 11:00, I say, "One more episode."
And then it's 12:00.
Every night?
Not every night.
Three nights a week, maybe four.
Five on bad weeks.
So, most nights.
Yes, most nights.
And what do you do after dinner?
I clean the kitchen.
I prepare my clothes for tomorrow and then I read or watch something very light for 30 minutes.
You prepare your clothes for tomorrow?
Yes, shoes, trousers, shirt, ready near the door.
So, your mornings are easy because your nights are organized.
Yes, that's the whole secret.
The morning starts the night before.
Say that again, slowly.
I want to write it down.
The morning starts the night before.
Okay, I'm writing.
Not on my hand.
So, what time do you go to bed?
I go to my room at 10:30 and I sleep by 11:00 and my phone stays outside the room.
Outside the room?
Outside the room, charging in the kitchen.
It's difficult for the first week and then it's normal.
What time do you sleep?
Around midnight, sometimes 1:00.
On Fridays, 2:00.
And I always say, "I'll fix it this weekend."
And then the weekend comes and I sleep until 11:00 and the circle continues.
That's called social jet lag.
Wait, what does that mean?
It means your sleep time changes a lot between work days and free days, like a small airplane trip without the airplane.
That's exactly what I do.
On Monday, I feel like I came back from another country and my passport is my phone.
How many hours do you sleep?
Six, maybe 5 and 1/2 on work days, 8 or 9 on Sunday.
So, you sleep badly and then you pay for it on Sunday.
Yes, and I know it's not healthy.
I know it.
But at 11:00 at night, my brain feels very alive.
My brain is alive at 7:00 in the morning.
We are different animals, Tina.
We are different animals.
So, let's talk about the weekend routine.
Is it very different for you?
Completely different. No alarm, I wake up naturally at 9:00 or 10:00 and then I have a slow morning.
Coffee and music and no plan.
No plan at all?
Maybe one thing.
Good food and clean clothes.
That's the whole goal.
My weekend is different.
I wake up at 7:00 because my body is used to it and then I feel a little angry because it's Saturday and my body doesn't know.
Your body is too professional.
My body is annoying.
So, I get up, I go to the market and I cook for the week.
And Sunday evening, do you feel that strange feeling?
What feeling?
The Sunday feeling, when the weekend is almost finished and your stomach feels a little strange.
Oh, I know that feeling very well.
To be honest, I prepare for Monday on Sunday evening.
I look at my week, I make a plan, and then I feel calm.
Calm? I feel not calm.
I feel like the weekend betrayed me.
So, on Monday morning, what is your advice for people listening?
I have one small advice.
Don't change your sleep time by more than 1 hour.
Not on Saturday, not on Sunday.
1 hour maximum?
1 hour maximum.
That way, Monday morning is not a shock.
And also, do one small thing for your future self every night.
Prepare your clothes, put your keys in the same place, wash the coffee cup.
Do one small thing for your future self.
That's beautiful.
It's simple, and it works.
Can I tell you my advice, too?
My advice is different.
Don't try to build a perfect routine.
Build a small one.
One thing you can do every day, even on a bad day.
Like what?
Like putting on the first shoe.
Like drinking water before coffee.
Small things are strong things.
I like that.
Small things are strong things.
Okay, so let's move to the next part.
We used a lot of useful words today.
A lot. My head is full.
Then let's slow down and look at the most useful ones.
You know, Leo, while we were talking, we used many useful words.
Let's look at them carefully.
Carefully. Slowly. My favorite speed.
First word, routine.
This means the things you do regularly in the same way, usually at the same time.
Oh, yes. And it's the perfect word for today.
My daily routine, my morning routine.
Exactly. For example, my morning routine starts at 6:00.
And you can also say, I have a simple routine.
I don't like changes.
What's your routine, Leo?
My routine is small.
Coffee, shower, keys, bus, but it works.
Next word, alarm.
This is the sound or the clock that wakes you up.
And we say set an alarm, not put an alarm.
That's a common mistake.
Exactly. For example, I set my alarm for 6:30.
And you can also say, my alarm didn't ring, so I was late.
Or the opposite, the alarm rang too early.
How many alarms do you set?
Four, but I'm trying to set one.
Tina is helping me, in theory.
Next word, commute.
This is the journey from home to work and from work to home.
Ah, so it's a noun.
My commute is 35 minutes.
Yes, and you can also say, I commute by bus.
Here, it's a verb.
For example, my commute is long, but I listen to podcasts.
And you can also say, I don't like the commute in winter.
Do you like your commute?
I do. I walk, so my commute is also my exercise.
Two things at one time.
Next word, habit.
This is something you do very often, sometimes without thinking.
Oh, yes. Good habit, bad habit.
Checking my phone is a bad habit.
Exactly. For example, eating at my desk is a bad habit.
And you can also say, it takes about a month to build a new habit.
What habit do you want to build?
I want to build the habit of putting my phone outside my bedroom, like you.
But my phone and I have a very close relationship.
Next word, productive.
This means you do a lot of useful work in your time.
So productive is about results, not about being busy.
Very important difference.
Busy means you have a lot to do.
Productive means you actually finish it.
For example, I'm more productive in the morning.
And you can also say, I had a very productive hour.
I finished everything.
When are you most productive?
After 5:00 when the office is quiet, and my best hour is the first hour after lunch, strangely.
Next word, exhausted.
This means extremely tired, not a little tired, very, very tired.
Ah, so tired is normal, and exhausted is maximum.
Exactly. For example, after the meeting, I was exhausted.
And you can also say, I feel exhausted, but I can't sleep.
When was the last time you felt exhausted?
Last Friday. I worked 8 hours and then I went to my friend's birthday party.
I was a very boring guest.
Next word, unwind.
This is a verb, it means to relax after work or stress.
Oh, I like this word.
It's like opening a rope, unwind.
That's exactly the image.
For example, I unwind by watching a show.
And you can also say, I need 30 minutes to unwind before dinner.
How do you unwind?
I walk home.
20 minutes of walking and my work day is finished in my head.
Next word, stay up.
This is a phrasal verb.
It means to go to bed later than usual or later than you should.
Ah, so this is my special skill.
I stayed up until 2:00.
Exactly. And the important part, after stay up, we use the simple form.
I stayed up to finish, not I stayed up to finishing.
For example, I stayed up late to finish a film.
And you can also say, don't stay up too late tonight.
Do you stay up late often?
Three or four nights a week, and every time I promise myself, tomorrow I sleep early.
And tomorrow, I don't.
Next word, oversleep.
This means to sleep longer than you planned and wake up late.
Oh, so this is different from stay up, right?
This is the morning problem.
Right. Stay up is the night, oversleep is the morning.
For example, I overslept and missed my bus.
And you can also say, I'm sorry I'm late.
I overslept. One sentence, not a documentary.
How many times did you oversleep this year?
Twice, or three times.
Okay, four. But one of those times was a very good dream.
Next word, in a rush.
This is a phrase.
It means you are moving fast because you are late or you have no time.
Oh, yes. I'm in a rush, not I have a rush.
That's a common mistake.
For example, I was in a rush, so I didn't eat breakfast.
And you can also say, sorry, I can't talk now.
I'm in a rush.
When are you in a rush?
Every morning between 7:15 and 7:40.
It's my daily sports event.
Next word, wind down.
This is a phrasal verb.
It means to slowly relax and get ready for sleep.
So, unwind is after work and wind down is before bed.
That's a nice simple way to remember it.
For example, I wind down with a book and a cup of tea.
And you can also say, I need an hour to wind down after a busy day.
What's your wind down routine?
I close my laptop at 9:00, then I wash my face, I read for 20 minutes, and I turn off the light by 11:00.
Next word, chores.
These are the small jobs at home.
Cleaning, washing dishes, shopping, laundry.
Oh, chores, my old friend.
For example, I do the chores on Saturday morning.
And you can also say, I hate doing chores, but I love a clean kitchen.
That's me.
What chores do you do?
Laundry and dishes.
I'm actually very good at dishes.
It's like meditation.
Warm water, quiet, thinking.
That's a nice way to see it.
Last word, used to.
This is a phrase for things you did in the past, but not now.
Ah, this one is important.
I used to wake up at 5:00.
Exactly. And the important part, after stay up, we use the simple form.
I stayed up to finish, not I stayed up to finishing.
For example, I stayed up late to finish a film.
And you can also say, I didn't used to sleep well.
For the negative, we drop the D.
What did you used to do that you don't do now?
I used to play football every Sunday.
Now, I watch football every Sunday with a bag of chips.
Life changes.
Okay, let's review the words, one line each.

Alarm, the sound or clock that wakes you up.
Commute, the journey between home and work.
Habit, something you do often, sometimes without thinking.
Productive, doing a lot of useful work.
Exhausted, extremely tired.
Unwind, to relax after work or stress.
Stay up, to go to bed later than usual.
Oversleep, to sleep longer than you planned.
In a rush, moving fast because you have no time.
Wind down, to slowly relax before sleep.
Chores, small jobs at home.
Used to, something you did in the past but not now.
13 words, and I remember most of them.
That's a good day for me.
Okay, Leo. That was a lot of talking about one single day.

We don't need the shower story.

Five parts, like five fingers.

I have toast and coffee.

I go to work by bus.

I arrive at 8:40.

I'm more productive in the morning.

I cook something simple.
I eat around 8.
I unwind by watching a show.

I put my phone outside the room.
I go to bed by 11.
I don't stay up late.

Five moments, and each moment needs maybe three sentences.
Exactly. And remember, you don't need perfect grammar.
You need time words.
First, then, after that, usually, sometimes, finally.
First, then, after that, finally.
I can say that in my sleep, which is ironic because I don't sleep.

This is our favorite part.
Our favorite part.
